# Replication crisis

## A crisis in psychology

![](media/replication_crisis1.png){.absolute top=150 left=-100 width="600" fig-alt="Manuscript info for Bem 2011 Feeling the Future: Experimental Evidence for Anomalous Retroactive Influences on Cognition and Affect"}

![](media/replication_crisis1b.png){.absolute top=150 left=550 width="600" fig-alt="Manuscript info for Wagenmakers et al. 2011 Why Psychologists Must Change the Way They Analyze Their Data: The Case of Psi: Comment on Bem (2011)"}

![](media/replication_crisis2.png){.absolute top=350 left=225 width="600" .fragment fig-alt="Manuscript info for Simmons et al. 2011 False-Positive Psychology: Undisclosed Flexibility in Data Collection and Analysis Allows Presenting Anything as Significant"}

## Replication in psychology

![Open Science Collaboration. (2015). Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science. _Science_. [doi:10.1126/science.aac4716](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aac4716)](media/replication.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Colored boxes showing number of replication studies whose outcomes matched the original's results. 39 studies matched and 61 studies did not. Colors represent the degree to which the replication results were similar to the original results."}

## Causes of the crisis

* Small sample sizes
* Optional stopping
* Poor understanding and use of statistics
* P-hacking
* HARKing
* Inconsistency in methods
* Bias against replications
* WEIRD populations

## A push for more reliable research

![](media/replicability_comp_psych.png){.absolute top=150 left=25 width="1000" fig-alt="Manuscript info for Stevens 2017: Replicability and Reproducibility in Comparative Psychology."}

## Measuring owner perceptions

### Dog Impulsivity Assessment Scale (DIAS)

::: {.fragment}
 * I would consider my dog to be very impulsive
 * My dog does not think before it acts
 * My dog appears to have a lot of control over how it responds
 * My dog is not very patient

[Wright et al., 2011](https://doi.org/10.46867/ijcp.2011.24.02.03)

:::

::: {.source}
[Stevens et al. 2022, _Animal Behavior & Cognition_](https://doi.org/10.26451/abc.09.03.02.2022)
:::

## Owners not good at predicting dog impulsivity {.center}


## Conclusions

Did not replicate Brady et al., 2018

::: {.incremental}
* British know their dogs better than Nebraskans?
* Different owner populations?
  - British vs. American dog-owner bonds
  - Demographics
* Different dog populations?
  - Breeds
  - Neuter status
:::


## Implications for reliability

::: {.incremental}
* Increase sample sizes
* Conduct more replications (within and between labs)
* Increase robustness and reproducibility of analyses
* Post data publicly
* Provide more and consistent info on owners
* Consider populations of owners and dogs
:::


# Aggregating studies

## Impulsivity as a trait in domestic dogs

::: {.callout-tip}
## Research Question

::: {style="font-size: 40px"}
::: {.fragment}
**Is impulsivity a behavioral trait in dogs?**
:::
::: {.fragment}
* Do dogs' impulsivity levels correlate across tasks?
* Do dogs' impulsivity levels correlate with owner perceptions?
:::
:::
:::

::: {.source}
[Barela et al. 2024, _Journal of Comparative Psychology_](https://doi.org/10.1037/com0000352)
:::


## Meta-analysis

:::{.incremental}
* Systematic review of the literature to extract and compare statistics from all published studies
* Searched 9,900 records from Scopus, Web of Science, and PsychINFO 
* 13 articles conducted correlations between impulsivity tasks and/or between the Dog Impulsivity Assessment Scale (DIAS) and behavioral tasks
:::

::: {.source}
[Barela et al. 2024, _Journal of Comparative Psychology_](https://doi.org/10.1037/com0000352)
:::

## Implications for reliability

::: {.incremental}
* Enhance statistical power
* Gives larger picture of effects
* Help resolve conflicting results
* Reduces biases toward positive effects
:::


# Big team science

## What is big team science?

> Collaborations wherein a comparatively large number of researchers pool their intellectual and/or material resources to pursue a common goal

---Baumgartner et al., 2023 _Royal Society Open Science_.

::: {.fragment}
![](media/psa_map.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="World map with pins showing locations of Psychological Science Accelerator research sites."}
:::

## Dogs follow the point

::: {.r-stack}
![](media/md1_overall_accuracy_0.png){fig-align="center" height="550" fig-alt="Plot of Accuracy as a function of Condition (Non-communicative and Communicative). There are no data."}

## Sites differ in owner age distribution

![](media/md1_owner_ages.png){fig-align="center" height="550" fig-alt="Panel of 17 histograms (one for each research site) showing frequency of participant owner ages across sites. :::

## Implications for reliability
::: {.incremental}
* Again, consider populations of owners and dogs
* Many analysts improved analysis

## What can you do?

::: {.incremental}
* Develop an [open science mindset](https://doi.org/10.1080/21642850.2021.2012474)
* Read articles about [easing into open science](https://doi.org/10.1525/collabra.18684)
* Propose to conduct replications or [meta-analysis](https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000351)
* Join the [Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science](https://improvingpsych.org/)
* Join a [big team science team](https://manydogsproject.github.io/getinvolved.html#other-big-team-science-groups)
* Learn R and/or Python
:::
